quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsui Mining & Smelting results briefing Q&A: Record of Briefing session Concerning FY2026 Q1 Results (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing record): Q1 FY2026 (April-June 2026) net sales were JPY201.6 billion, operating income JPY21 billion, ordinary income JPY23.5 billion and net income attributable to owners of parent JPY16.8 billion; YoY, group sales increased by JPY32.6 billion, driven by higher sales volumes of key engineered materials products such as the ultra-thin copper foil MicroThin and the electrolytic copper foil VSP for AI servers, plus the weaker yen and improved metal prices in the metals segment.

quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsui Mining & Smelting results briefing Q&A: Record of Briefing session Concerning FY2026 Q1 Results (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing record): after reviewing Q1 results and business trends from Q2 onward, the company now expects FY2026 net sales of JPY850 billion, operating income of JPY94 billion, ordinary income of JPY100 billion and net income of JPY80 billion, all above the forecasts disclosed on May 13; operating income is expected at JPY45 billion in H1 (JPY4 billion below the previous forecast, as copper-foil gains are outweighed by a metals-segment decline) and JPY49 billion in H2 (JPY7 billion above, mainly on higher MicroThin sales volume). Price assumptions for Q2 onward: LME zinc USD3,400, lead USD1,900, copper USD6.12, JPY160 to the US dollar.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 forecast: net sales JPY850 billion; operating income JPY94 billion (H1 JPY45 billion, H2 JPY49 billion); ordinary income JPY100 billion; net income JPY80 billion

quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsui Mining & Smelting results briefing Q&A: Record of Briefing session Concerning FY2026 Q1 Results (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing record): the company announced plans to expand production capacity for its core copper foil products VSP, MicroThin and FaradFlex through investments totaling JPY42 billion by 2030, to capture medium- to long-term demand in AI servers, telecommunications infrastructure, optical modules, semiconductor packaging and printed circuit boards; MicroThin capacity in 2030 rises from the originally planned 5.6 million square meters to 8 million square meters, and depending on sales volume its 2030 results could exceed expectations. Management called this a significant step toward the 2030 operating profit targets of JPY130 billion for engineered materials and JPY150 billion company-wide, and said it continues to explore new in-house factories and M&A for demand after 2030. For the expansion it expects an operation rate of around 80% (previous benchmark for considering expansion: around 70%).
quarterly_data.figure: JPY42 billion by 2030; monthly capacity VSP 720 to 1,400 metric tons, MicroThin 4.9 million to 8 million square meters, FaradFlex 75,000 to 355,000 square meters

quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsui Mining & Smelting results briefing Q&A: Record of Briefing session Concerning FY2026 Q1 Results (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): demand for MicroThin in optical transceiver applications has grown more strongly than initially anticipated; at the previous forecast the company expected FY2026 optical-transceiver sales volume of approximately 200,000-250,000 square meters per month and now expects the FY2026 average to exceed 600,000 square meters per month. MicroThin is currently used in almost all 800G optical transceivers and is expected to continue in next-generation 1.6T transceivers; management does not expect a shift from the Modified Semi-Additive Process (MSAP) to the Semi-Additive Process (SAP) as generations advance to 1.6T and 2.4T, so MicroThin volumes can grow with the number of optical transceivers.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 MicroThin optical-transceiver volume expected to exceed 600,000 square meters per month (previous forecast approximately 200,000-250,000 square meters per month)

quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsui Mining & Smelting results briefing Q&A: Record of Briefing session Concerning FY2026 Q1 Results (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing record and Q&A): since the start of FY2026, actual demand for MicroThin and VSP copper foil for AI servers has been even stronger than last year. For MicroThin, HDI demand is unchanged from the previous forecast while PKG demand is extremely strong, particularly for server memory applications, so H1 and H2 volume forecasts were revised up, with some seasonal moderation factored into H2 because it is uncertain whether the strength continues to fiscal year-end. VSP volumes are expected below the previous forecast because customer qualification of products from the Malaysia Plant is delayed relative to expectations; management says the equipment ramp-up is on plan with no quality issues, views it as a procedural delay with no particular market-share impact, and sees upside if qualification progresses smoothly. FaradFlex demand is increasing rapidly in AI infrastructure, mainly for switches in AI servers, adopted faster than anticipated; management sees it as complementary to MLCCs.

quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsui Mining & Smelting results briefing Q&A: Record of Briefing session Concerning FY2026 Q1 Results (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A) on copper foil pricing and earnings: VSP price increases took effect from October 2025 and an additional increase from July 2026, applied selectively where demand is particularly strong rather than uniformly across grades; at present no specific plans for further MicroThin price increases, though further increases will be considered given elevated copper prices, costs and supply-demand. In the upward revision of copper foil earnings, sales-volume changes contribute approximately JPY4.0 billion and price increases approximately JPY3.5 billion (MicroThin approximately JPY3.0 billion, VSP approximately JPY0.5-1.0 billion), higher copper prices raise raw material costs by approximately JPY2.5 billion, inventory and foreign exchange are each approximately JPY1.0 billion favorable, and most of the remaining approximately JPY3.0 billion is FaradFlex. Management expects copper-foil ROIC to stay broadly in line with the FY2030 target of 64%.
quarterly_data.figure: Volume approximately JPY4.0 billion; price increases approximately JPY3.5 billion; raw materials approximately -JPY2.5 billion; ROIC target 64% (FY2030)

quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsui Mining & Smelting results briefing Q&A: Record of Briefing session Concerning FY2026 Q1 Results (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): super-high-grade VSP products of HVLP4 and higher are expected to account for approximately 45% of VSP sales volume in H1 (previous forecast approximately 40%) and approximately 60% in H2 (unchanged). Competitors are entering as demand expands across HVLP categories and the company is not aggressively pursuing lower categories, so some change has occurred there; in the higher HVLP categories management sees few competitors able to produce with consistent quality, no significant change in the competitive landscape, and believes the company remains the leading supplier (company's claim).
quarterly_data.figure: HVLP4-and-higher share of VSP volume: approximately 45% (H1), approximately 60% (H2)

quarterly_data.quarter: Mitsui Mining & Smelting results briefing Q&A: Record of Briefing session Concerning FY2026 Q1 Results (08-07-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing record) segment outlook: engineered materials ordinary income is forecast at JPY39 billion for H1 and JPY78 billion for FY2026 (initial full-year forecast JPY67 billion), on higher MicroThin and VSP volumes partly offset by lower catalyst profits from falling precious metal prices; exhaust gas catalysts for motorcycles remain strong, and despite challenges in China automotive, full-year catalyst volumes are expected in line with the initial forecast. Metals segment ordinary income is expected to fall JPY5.4 billion YoY to JPY13 billion in H1 and JPY48.6 billion to JPY26.5 billion for the full year (initial forecast JPY37.5 billion), reflecting zinc/lead costs including a major maintenance shutdown, smaller copper/gold/silver volume variances at the Okayama smelter and lower gold and silver prices; assumptions from Q2 onward are gold USD4,200/oz and silver USD65/oz (start of year: USD4,800/oz and USD80/oz).
quarterly_data.figure: Engineered materials ordinary income JPY39 billion (H1), JPY78 billion (FY); Metals ordinary income JPY13 billion (H1), JPY26.5 billion (FY)
